---
title: "Trip options"
description: >
  peabiru's own trip planner: every trip worth considering between two
  points, on time, fare, transfers and walking, with the legs of each.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

`trip_options()` is peabiru's own trip planner, with no counterpart in r5r:
for each origin and destination it gives every trip worth considering, the
ones that no other trip beats on all the chosen criteria at once. Where
`detailed_itineraries()` answers "what is the fastest way there?",
`trip_options()` answers "what are my choices?": faster but dearer, cheaper
but slower, fewer transfers, less walking.

## Not dominated

A trip *dominates* another when it is no worse on every chosen criterion and
better on at least one. The criteria are

- `"TIME"`: door-to-door minutes from the departure minute, waits included;
- `"FARE"`: the fare by a fare structure (see `vignette("fares")`);
- `"TRANSFERS"`: rides minus one; a trip without public transport has 0, as
  many as a trip with a single ride;
- `"WALK"`: minutes on foot: the access and egress legs when they are
  walked, and the walks between stops (a bicycle or car leg counts 0).

By default all four are used with a fare structure, all but `"FARE"`
without one. At each departure minute of the window the options are the
exact set of trips not dominated, with one trip per combination of values.
The trips are those of r5r's network semantics (the same access and egress
searches, transfers between stops and boarding rules as
`detailed_itineraries()`), so the times agree with the other functions.

The example uses r5r's sample data of Porto Alegre, whose GTFS has
timetables, and the fare structure r5r ships for it, downloaded once into
the temporary directory.

```{r data}
poa <- r5r_sample()
poa_network <- build_network(poa, n_threads = 2)
fares_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "fares_poa.zip")
if (!file.exists(fares_zip)) {
  download.file(paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/",
                       "inst/extdata/poa/fares/fares_poa.zip"),
                fares_zip, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}
fares <- read_fare_structure(fares_zip)
origin <- data.frame(id = "89a90128053ffff", lat = -30.0722552482611, lon = -51.1863771572777)
destination <- data.frame(id = "89a90129c9bffff", lat = -30.0511737750423, lon = -51.1733521719011)
```

## Time and fare

With time and fare as the criteria, the options over the ten minutes from
14:00 trade minutes for reais:

```{r time-fare}
res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure,
                    criteria = c("TIME", "FARE"), fare_structure = fares,
                    n_threads = 2)
res$options[, c("option", "total_time", "fare", "transfers", "walk_time",
                "departure_time", "n_departures", "description")]
```

Each row is an *option*: trips with the same street modes, the same routes
between the same stops, and the same fare, transfers and minutes on foot,
found at `n_departures` of the window's minutes. Its total time changes with
the minute (the wait at the start does), so the row reports the trip of its
best minute, `departure_time`. Over the whole window an option can look
dominated by another that was not available at its own minutes;
`by_departure = TRUE` adds the frontier of every minute:

```{r by-departure}
res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 3L,
                    criteria = c("TIME", "FARE"), fare_structure = fares,
                    by_departure = TRUE, itineraries = FALSE, n_threads = 2)
res$departures
```

## All four criteria and the legs

With the default criteria (all four, since there is a fare structure) the
trade-offs with transfers and walking come in too. The legs of each option
are in `itineraries`, in the format of `detailed_itineraries()` and keyed by
`from_id`, `to_id` and `option`: an `sf` of lines, or a `data.frame` with
`drop_geometry = TRUE`.

```{r legs}
res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure, fare_structure = fares,
                    drop_geometry = TRUE, n_threads = 2)
nrow(res$options)
legs <- res$itineraries
legs[legs$option == 1, c("segment", "mode", "cumulative_fare",
                         "segment_duration", "wait", "distance", "route")]
```

`max_options` keeps the first options of each pair, `max_fare` and
`max_trip_duration` leave out the trips beyond them, and
`itineraries = FALSE` skips the legs. `output_dir` writes one CSV file per
pair instead.

## Fares are not additive

A fare is not the sum of its rides: a transfer within the time allowance is
discounted, some types have unlimited transfers, a cap may apply. Two
partial trips are only compared on fare when one is at least as cheap for
every way both can continue; the comparison makes no assumption about the
fare structure (a discounted transfer may even cost more than two full
fares). This exactness has a price: partial trips that could still get a
discount are kept apart until they cannot, which makes the fare criterion
the slowest one.

## Frequency-based routes

GTFS `frequencies.txt` gives a headway, not departure times. r5r draws
random departures (Monte Carlo); `trip_options()` does not: a
frequency-based vehicle is boarded at its expected time, half a headway
after the traveller is ready to board (or after the period starts), within
the period, and with `exact_times = 1` at the first scheduled departure.
The results do not change from call to call, and differ on purpose from
r5r's draws. The Sao Paulo sample shipped with the package runs by
frequency:

```{r frequencies}
res <- trip_options(network, points[1, ], points[27, ],
                    departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 5L,
                    itineraries = FALSE, n_threads = 2)
res$options[, c("option", "total_time", "transfers", "walk_time",
                "n_departures", "description")]
```

## Compared with r5r's functions

- `pareto_frontier()` (r5r's) gives, for each fare cutoff, the percentiles
  of the travel time over Monte Carlo draws of departure times: a summary of
  time against budget, without the trips.
- `detailed_itineraries()` (r5r's) gives the fastest trip, or with
  `shortest_path = FALSE` R5's alternatives (one per sequence of routes,
  the fastest of each).
- `trip_options()` gives the trade-offs themselves, trip by trip, with their
  legs, on any of four criteria. With `criteria = "TIME"` and
  `time_window = 1`, its first option has the total time of
  `detailed_itineraries()`'s fastest trip for that minute.
